sensory.aromaNotes: Characteristic pine, cinnamon, and spicy notes (matsutake alcohol / related volatiles); prized as a flavor, not a neutral protein
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Obligate ectomycorrhizal; fruiting bodies are not farmed at industrial scale. Firm stipe tissue is meaty in the culinary sense, but supply and price rule it out as analog bulk. The only plausible alt-protein role is a high-value aroma extract or limited mycelial flavor work — still research-scale.
sensory.preparationContext: Wild-harvested fruiting bodies, grilled or in soup; not a fermentation protein
sensory.confidenceNotes: Culinary flavor is undisputed. Do not list matsutake as a scalable mycoprotein.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: Convex to umbonate pileus on a thick fibrous stipe; white gills; often with pine-duff debris at the base
morphology.microscopyNotes: Ectomycorrhizal; no industrial fruiting-body farm exists

nutrition.preparationContext: Wild fruiting-body ranges from edible-mushroom reviews
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Not a protein-spec ingredient. Values are order-of-magnitude only.

geographic.nativeRange: East Asia, and related pine forests in western North America / Scandinavia (closely related taxa)
geographic.cultivatedRegions: Not commercially cultivated as fruiting bodies; harvest is wild
geographic.habitat: Ectomycorrhizal with pine and related conifers

strains.availabilityNotes: Mycorrhizal isolates exist; there is no production strain for fruiting-body biomass.

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Luxury wild mushroom. Alt-protein relevance is flavor (pine/spicy/umami), not protein tonnage. Treat as a seasoning analog, not a Quorn-class biomass.
commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Traditional food; supply is ecological, not industrial.

regulatory.notes: Traditional wild edible. Look-alikes in Tricholoma include toxic species; any product use needs identity control.

altProteinResearch.title: Edible mushrooms: chemical composition and nutritional value
altProteinResearch.summary: Frames matsutake as a wild edible with distinctive aroma — relevant to flavor design, not industrial mycoprotein.
